title: Unique identifier linking during account registration
description: Homeowner provides unique identifiers (username, email, device ID) during account registration that can be used to link all subsequent data flows to this specific individual
assumptions: Registration process requires unique account identification

title: Identifier processing during registration
description: Homeowner's unique identifiers are processed and stored during account registration, creating a persistent link to their identity
assumptions: Registration requires unique account identification

title: Sensitive data type collection
description: Homeowner may provide camera/sensor data that is more sensitive than functionally required for basic account registration
assumptions: Registration process may collect device capabilities beyond what's needed

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Homeowner may not be fully aware of how their registration data and device information will be processed, stored, and potentially shared
assumptions: Registration process may not provide clear information about data processing purposes

title: Data minimization violation
description: Registration process may collect more personal data than functionally needed for account creation and device enrollment
assumptions: Registration may collect unnecessary device capabilities or personal information

title: Quasi-identifier linking through registration data
description: Registration data combined with device enrollment data can serve as quasi-identifiers to link camera/sensor data to the homeowner
assumptions: Registration data includes attributes that can be combined with device data

title: Excessive data treatment and analysis
description: Home Hub may analyze and enrich registration and device data beyond what is functionally needed for the enrollment process
assumptions: System may perform additional data processing beyond basic storage

title: Lack of data subject control over preferences
description: Homeowner may not have control over how their registration and device data is processed, stored, or shared
assumptions: System may not provide granular consent controls for data processing

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: System may lack adequate support for data subject rights such as access, rectification, and erasure of registration data
assumptions: System may not implement full GDPR-style data subject rights

title: Linking through unique identifier in camera data
description: Camera clips may contain unique identifiers (timestamps, device IDs, location data) that can be used to link video data to specific individuals or households.
assumptions: Assumes camera system captures identifiable metadata

title: Processing of unique identifier in video data
description: Home Hub processes video data containing unique references to the identity of the data subject (e.g., device ID, timestamp, location).
assumptions: Assumes camera system captures identifiable metadata

title: Collection of more sensitive data types than functionally required
description: Camera system may collect more sensitive data types (e.g., full video footage, audio) than functionally required for the stated purpose.
assumptions: Assumes video upload is for security monitoring

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combining data of single individual
description: Video metadata combined with other data (timestamps, location, device ID) can serve as quasi-identifiers to link video data to specific individuals.
assumptions: Assumes metadata contains multiple attributes

title: Identified information in metadata
description: Metadata of video files in transit may contain identified information (timestamps, device IDs, location data) that can be used to identify the data subject.
assumptions: Assumes metadata is transmitted with video data

title: Excessive volume of personal data processed
description: Cloud storage may process excessive volume of video data beyond what is functionally needed for the stated purpose.
assumptions: Assumes video retention exceeds functional requirements

title: Duration/retention of personal data longer than needed
description: Cloud storage may retain video data longer than functionally needed for the stated purpose.
assumptions: Assumes retention policy exceeds functional requirements

title: Revealing attributes in stored video data
description: Cloud storage processes video data containing revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Assumes video contains identifiable content

title: Linking through motion alert metadata
description: Motion alert data in transit may contain metadata (timestamps, device identifiers, location coordinates) that can be used to link the alert to a specific individual or household, enabling cross-referencing with other data sources.
assumptions: Assumes motion alerts may include device identifiers or location data that could be used for linking purposes.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if motion alerts include identifying metadata - depends on implementation details.

title: Identifying information in motion alert
description: Home Hub may include identifying information (device ID, user identifier, location) in the motion alert that allows identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Assumes motion alerts may contain device or user identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if motion alerts include identifying information - depends on Home Hub implementation.

title: Potentially unnecessary data types in motion alert
description: Home Hub may include more sensitive data types in the motion alert than functionally required for the alerting purpose (e.g., detailed location coordinates, device specifications).
assumptions: Assumes motion alert functionality may include more data than strictly necessary for the alerting purpose.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain what data is included in motion alerts - depends on Home Hub implementation.

title: Excessive party exposure of motion alerts
description: Mobile App Backend may make motion alerts accessible to more parties than functionally necessary (e.g., sharing with analytics services, third-party integrations).
assumptions: Assumes Mobile App Backend may share motion alert data with additional services beyond the core functionality.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain what data is shared by Mobile App Backend - depends on backend implementation.

title: Unawareness of motion alert processing
description: Users may not be aware that their motion data is being collected, processed, and forwarded to the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Assumes users may not be fully informed about the data processing activities related to motion alerts.
uncertainty_note: Depends on user notification practices and privacy policies.

title: Profiling of individuals from aggregated analytics
description: The cloud analytics vendor may analyze device-usage patterns to infer individual behaviors, preferences, or characteristics, even from aggregated data, potentially enabling re-identification or creating detailed user profiles.
assumptions: Aggregation does not guarantee anonymity; patterns may still be identifiable

title: User unawareness of data sharing with external vendor
description: Mobile app users may not be aware that their device-usage analytics are being shared with an external cloud analytics vendor, violating transparency requirements.
assumptions: Users may not have visibility into third-party data sharing practices

title: Lack of user control over data sharing preferences
description: Users may not have meaningful control or consent mechanisms to opt-out of sharing device-usage analytics with the cloud analytics vendor.
assumptions: The app may not provide granular privacy controls for third-party data sharing

title: Data shared with predetermined external party
description: Personal data is made accessible to a predetermined external party (cloud analytics vendor) that is known and fixed, potentially exceeding functional necessity.
assumptions: The vendor is a known external entity, not a necessary party for core app functionality

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Device-usage analytics may be more personal data than functionally required for the stated purpose of the mobile app, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: The analytics may not be strictly necessary for the app's core functionality
uncertainty_note: Uncertain whether the analytics are strictly necessary for stated app purposes

title: Video data contains unique identifiers for linking
description: The stored video clip may contain unique identifiers (user ID, timestamp, location) that can be used to link the homeowner to other data sources or profiles.
assumptions: Video metadata typically includes identifying information

title: Processing of identified video data
description: The cloud storage system processes and stores video data that contains identified information about the homeowner.
assumptions: Video files contain identifying metadata

title: Unnecessary data types disclosed
description: The video storage may disclose more sensitive data types than functionally required for playback (e.g., full video metadata, timestamps, location data).
assumptions: Video storage includes comprehensive metadata

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combining
description: Video metadata (timestamps, location, user ID) in transit could be combined with other data to link the homeowner to other activities or profiles.
assumptions: Video metadata includes quasi-identifiers

title: Identified information in metadata
description: The data flow may involve metadata containing identified information about the homeowner (user ID, timestamps, location).
assumptions: Video transmission includes metadata

title: Processing of unique identifier data
description: The mobile app backend processes video data containing unique identifiers that can be traced back to the homeowner.
assumptions: Video playback requires user identification

title: Unnecessary treatment of video data
description: The mobile app may perform additional analysis or enrichment on the video data beyond what is needed for playback functionality.
assumptions: App may analyze video content beyond playback

title: Lack of data subject control over preferences
description: The homeowner may not have control over how their video data is processed, stored, or disclosed by the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Limited user control over data processing preferences
